intent: Draw the framed surface of a bubble that holds the turn's text or rich content, optionally as a link or button.
typical_uses: The text of one conversation turn inside a Bubble
A clickable bubble, such as a suggestion the user can pick, rendered as a button or a link

dont_use_when.situation: A clickable action that is not a turn in a conversation

invariants.text: The pointer cursor, the hover fill and the focus ring apply only when the rendered element is a `button` or an `a` (bubble.module.css `.bubbleContent:is(button, a)`); the default div gets none of them and is not focusable.
The surface is capped at its Bubble's width, breaks long unbroken words (`overflow-wrap: break-word`) and clips anything that still overflows (`overflow: hidden`).

anti_patterns.dont: Attach an onClick to the default div to make a bubble clickable
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `render={<button type="button" />}` or a link element, which is focusable and gets the kit's hover and focus styling

a11y.by: bubble.test.tsx asserts that BubbleContent rendered with `render={<button type="button" />}` is found by role "button" with the accessible name "Click here" and keeps the content class

rtl.by: bubble.module.css `.bubbleContent:is(button, a)` sets the physical `text-align: left`, so a clickable bubble's text does not mirror under a right-to-left direction

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (BubbleContent passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

good.title: A suggestion the user can pick
good.code:
<Bubble variant="outline">
  <BubbleContent render={<button type="button" onClick={onPick} />}>Show me the diff</BubbleContent>
</Bubble>

bad.title: A clickable div
bad.why: The default div is not focusable and exposes no button role, and the kit's pointer cursor, hover fill and focus ring apply only to a rendered button or link.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (BubbleContent passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.
